data.exact_reserve_text: The 2018 YOA result has improved by 9.3% in calendar year 2020, notwithstanding strengthening of reserves in respect of unexpired political risk policies exposed to worsening global economic conditions. Favourable runoff experience and reserve releases in the year across all classes except the Political Risk and Director & Officers classes. Strengthening of Political Risk reserves as a consequence of specific adverse experience and a reevaluation of reserves in the light of the deterioration in global economic conditions which occurred during 2020.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Strengthening of Political Risk reserves as a consequence of specific adverse experience and a re-evaluation of reserves in light of the deterioration in global economic conditions during 2020.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2020 gross claims outstanding were GBP 114.931m. During 2020 there was a small net favourable prioryear development (approximately a GBP 0.8m gross release,  -0.7% of opening reserves), driven by favourable runoff and reserve releases across most classes, partly offset by reserve strengthening in Political Risk (and D&O) due to specific adverse experience and deterioration in global economic conditions. The year also included reinsurance-to-close activity and restructuring noted by management which affects the closed year outcome.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development was not stated as a single gross movement in a dedicated 'movement in prior years' note. The PYD figure was calculated from the published gross claims development triangle (development diagonal comparison) and is a small net release (-GBP 0.816m). The year-end RITC and closure activity (2018 YOA) are material contextual items and could distort development comparisons; use caution interpreting the triangle.
